By discretizing the PHX, this method can capture rapidly changing fluid properties, e.g., phase change, as they progress through the heat exchanger. For this work, we discretized the PHX into 100 sub-heat exchangers to ensure that PCMs latent heat properties were captured during the PHX design and performance calculations. For this work, we assumed a fraction of installation and labor as 2% and 3%, respectively. 1.5 PCM Salt Slurry Properties For this work, we assumed the PCM particles were suspended within a salt slurry where the salt was assumed to be the 3rd generation molten salts (i.e., 45.98% MgCl2, 38.91% KCl, 15.11% NaCl). Previous experimental work on this composition of molten salt was used to estimate the thermophysical properties of the salt (Wang et al.). The property correlations determined by Wang et al. were extrapolated to 750°C for this work. However, it is unclear if this molten salt composition is stable up to 750°C and more experimental work would be required to determine the salt’s stability at these temperatures. The PCMs particle properties for this work were characterized by PowderMet Inc. The PCM particles are formed by various compositions of aluminum, silicon, magnesium, and copper. The specific compositions of each PCM investigated were determined by PowderMet Inc. Table 2 presents the three PCMs that were investigated, which includes the estimated heat of fusion, temperature range of phase change, and proposed element compositions.
